inspection_summary: All 850 logical lines were inspected. The source links large values of ζ on the critical line to an extremal GCD quadratic form through a modified resonance method. A multiplicative weight on carefully restricted square-free integers creates a nearly maximal GCD sum; divisor-closed truncation preserves most mass; multiplicative clustering converts that arithmetic structure into a long Dirichlet resonator; and positivity of a smoothing transform lets a selected subcollection supply the lower bound while separate estimates control normalization and the excluded low-frequency range. The paper also makes its limitation explicit: the available GCD upper bound constrains further improvement within this resonance architecture. Prose and logical structure are well preserved, but square roots are often rendered as isolated p glyphs, displayed sums and products have disrupted reading order, and thresholds, subscripts, iterated logarithms, and Fourier normalizations require verification against the raw PDF before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Extreme ζ values are reduced to a near-optimal GCD sum
accepted_units.why_material: The main theorem improves the scale of known lower bounds for |ζ(1/2+it)|, and the introduction identifies the new causal ingredient: a large GCD form inserted into Soundararajan's resonance method, with optimality of the GCD exponent as a parallel consequence.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem, historical comparison, resonance declaration, GCD upper bound, and claimed optimality belong together because they define both the gain and its controlling resource.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Radicals, asymptotic exponents, the zeta argument, and the GCD sum are layout-degraded; exact constants and ranges must be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A weighted GCD quadratic form supplies an essentially optimal resonator
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 allows optimized positive coefficients rather than uniform weights, situates the form in the GCD-sum hierarchy, and explains that nearly extremal square-free sets are enough to produce an essentially optimal resonating Dirichlet polynomial even without identifying an exact extremizer.
accepted_units.context_note: The weighted theorem, matrix viewpoint, historical σ-regimes, and near-extremizer interpretation are retained as one structural unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The kernel gcd(nk,nℓ)/√(nknℓ), powers, and exponential scale are visually fragmented; verify the exact normalization and constants in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The same resonator predicts a smooth transition across vertical lines
accepted_units.why_material: The authors explain how their resonance variant extends to 1/2<σ<1 and predict how the smoothness profile of an optimal resonator changes as σ moves between endpoint regimes.
accepted_units.context_note: This is strategic perspective rather than a proof in this paper and is retained because it identifies which representation feature should vary with σ.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The νσ asymptotics and endpoint arrows are extraction-sensitive; exact formulas require the PDF. The detailed proof is explicitly deferred to later work, so the claim here is a reported method prediction, not established local evidence.

accepted_units.title: Prime-local weights factor the GCD objective into an Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: The proof chooses a controlled band of primes, defines a multiplicative function on square-free integers, rewrites the weighted GCD form into divisor sums, and factorizes the normalized quantity into local prime contributions; two lemmas then isolate size and truncation obligations.
accepted_units.context_note: The prime set, weight f(p), divisor-sum rewrite, Euler product, and two reduction lemmas must remain together to expose the design rather than just its result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining interval for primes, f(p), nested divisor sums, and Euler factors contain broken radicals and line ordering; exact symbolic use requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Taking logarithms turns the Euler product gain into a prime-density integral
accepted_units.why_material: Small local weights permit logarithmic linearization of the Euler product, and a prime-number-theorem approximation converts the accumulated gain over the chosen prime band into the target iterated-logarithm exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: This short proof is a reusable compression from multiplicative local design to a global asymptotic payoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-root prefactor, integration limits, and iterated logarithms are heavily line-broken; the transformation is clear but constants need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Occupancy caps compress an infinite multiplicative support to at most N integers
accepted_units.why_material: Primes are partitioned into scale blocks, numbers with excessive occupancy in any block are removed, and factorial/binomial estimates show that the remaining square-free support is divisor closed and has cardinality at most N.
accepted_units.context_note: The block definition, occupancy threshold, divisor closure, and entropy-style cardinality estimate form one compression mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Block endpoints, occupancy thresholds, floors, products, and binomial estimates are extraction-sensitive; exact inequalities and exponents require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: An exponential tilt proves the discarded multiplicative mass is negligible
accepted_units.why_material: A union bound reduces discarded mass to blockwise tails; inserting a tilt b>1, factorizing over primes, and balancing its gain against the occupancy penalty yields a negative exponent and proves the truncation preserves the Euler-product main term.
accepted_units.context_note: The tail decomposition, tilted product, local square-mass estimate, and choice b−1−a log b<0 are one concentration argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested sums, products, and exponents are densely fragmented; the sign-selection mechanism is readable, but exact factors must be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Spectral comparison transfers a weighted extremizer to unweighted GCD configurations
accepted_units.why_material: The paper compares the uniform GCD average Γ(N) with the optimized quadratic form Λ(N); a known inequality between them converts Theorem 2 into arbitrarily large unweighted examples and proves the upper-bound exponent cannot be below one.
accepted_units.context_note: The two extremal quantities, comparison inequality, subsequence conclusion, and monotonicity caveat are kept together because they explain exactly what is and is not transferred.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definitions of Γ and Λ and the maxima over n≤N are visually misaligned; exact constants and quantifiers require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Multiplicative ratios, not integer size, determine the resonator geometry
accepted_units.why_material: The resonance ratio reduces a pointwise maximum to two smoothed moments. The key design abandons matching the zeta approximant's length: logarithmically close elements of the long multiplicative set are clustered, and their squared weights are aggregated into a short enough Dirichlet polynomial because relevant frequencies depend on m/n.
accepted_units.context_note: The moment ratio, positivity requirements on the smoother, frequency explanation, clustering rule, and coefficient aggregation together define the modified resonator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier notation, interval intersections, M′, and the square-root definition of r(m) are broken across lines; exact construction requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Large divisor ratios contribute negligibly to the resonator's arithmetic mass
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3 rewrites the unwanted divisor range by complementary divisors and uses a fractional-power penalty plus multiplicativity to show it is uniformly negligible over the compressed support.
accepted_units.context_note: The reindexing and multiplicative product estimate are retained with the lemma because they justify later restricting to frequency-compatible divisors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The divisor thresholds, fractional powers, and final Euler product are extraction-sensitive; verify exact exponents in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Frequency spacing controls the excluded low-height interval
accepted_units.why_material: An oscillatory-integral estimate gives the minimum of interval length and inverse frequency; separating near, medium, and far multiplicative ratios then bounds the part of the zeta-resonator integral below the target height.
accepted_units.context_note: The base oscillatory estimate, dyadic-like ratio shells, and summed bound form one range-separation mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logarithmic denominator, shell definition, and integral bounds are visually fragmented; exact constants and endpoints require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fast Fourier decay bounds the resonator's normalization cost
accepted_units.why_material: Expanding the smoothed square of the resonator converts the denominator moment into a Fourier-weighted pair sum; frequency clustering and rapid decay suppress separated pairs and bound nearby pairs by the total multiplicative mass.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the cost side of the resonance ratio and must be represented separately from the gain side.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Fourier-transform normalization, Gaussian factors, and pair restrictions are extraction-sensitive; exact powers of log T require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Positivity selects arithmetic coincidences that reproduce the large GCD sum
accepted_units.why_material: A classical finite Dirichlet approximation to ζ turns the numerator moment into a positive triple sum. Positivity permits restriction to multiplicative coincidences, clustering and Cauchy–Schwarz recover weighted divisor pairs, tail lemmas replace them by the full GCD quantity, and the numerator/denominator ratio yields the extreme-value theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The zeta approximation, low-range removal, positive Fourier sum, selected subcollection, GCD comparison, and final ratio are one complete gain mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This span contains dense triple sums, Fourier factors, ratio constraints, and asymptotic exponents; the strategic chain is prose-supported, but every exact formula should be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The GCD upper bound is a ceiling for this resonance architecture
accepted_units.why_material: The authors trace cardinality restrictions and the crucial numerator estimate back to the GCD upper bound and conclude that only a modest constant improvement is available without changing the method.
accepted_units.context_note: This source-specific negative result prevents interpreting the successful resonator as an open-ended route to arbitrary improvements.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: No material extraction defect beyond ordinary mathematical symbols; the limitation is explicit in prose.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic similarity becomes spectral resonance
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A GCD kernel measures multiplicative overlap among square-free integers; clustering preserves the ratios encoding that overlap, and the resonator converts those ratios into frequencies whose positive contribution amplifies a smoothed zeta moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact numerical gain depends on formula-sensitive normalizations and on cited resonance estimates, so raw-PDF verification is required.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Near extremality by local design plus global compression
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Prime-local weights create Euler-product gain, while blockwise occupancy caps and exponential tilting compress the infinite support without losing the mass that drives the extremal form.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper constructs a nearly maximal family rather than characterizing an actual extremizer.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A weighted extremizer can certify an unweighted obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Comparing optimized and uniform quadratic forms converts a weighted lower bound into arbitrarily large unweighted configurations, proving that the exponent in the general GCD upper bound cannot be improved below one.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The argument first produces a subsequence; a stronger all-large-N statement needs monotonicity machinery deliberately omitted here.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Proof-budget separation reveals the resonance bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof succeeds by separately budgeting low-height oscillation, denominator normalization, and positive numerator gain; after those losses are controlled, the remaining ceiling is the available GCD-sum bound rather than smoothing or truncation throughput.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a solver-architecture-specific obstruction: a materially different method need not inherit the same ceiling.
